newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Dec 31.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
Sales of computers by the Great Wall Group are seen reaching 200,000 units in 1996. The group's assets are now worth 2.71 billion yuan.
The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China signs a contract to act as a life insurance agent for the People's Insurance Company of China.
Postal savings reached 207.8 billion yuan at the end of November, up 46.2 billion yuan from the same period in 1995.

A new set of quarantine regulations will go into effect on January 1. The new rules will require Chinese traders to submit samples of imports and get approval from quarantine authorities before signing contracts.
Fears over Britain's mad cow disease send Chinese beef exports soaring as Hong Kong and Southeast Asian markets search for alternative sources of supply.
The gross output value of China's mining industry is expected to rise by 25 percent from last year, with output of mineral ore is seen up six percent.
The Chinese General Association of Textile Industry decides to take 3.4 million spindles out of operation after previous cuts of five million spindles.
